questions.question: Why does the Born (on-shell) decay rate fail near decay thresholds?

options.b: the two-magnon continuum has van Hove edges: Γ_Born is singular there and can exceed ε

questions.question: What is the iΓ approximation?

options.b: internal magnons carry their own damping: ω − ε_q − ε_{k−q} + i(Γ_q + Γ_{k−q})/2, iterated to self-consistency

questions.question: Why must the grid be closed (unshifted)?

options.b: k, q and k−q must all be grid points, so the internal widths Γ_q are known

questions.explanation: Off-grid momenta (e.g. a band path) use periodic interpolation of the converged grid widths.

questions.question: Why is the energy kept at the 1/S on-shell value instead of solving the Dyson equation off-shell?

options.b: off-shell Re Σ mixes orders in 1/S and breaks the Hartree–Fock/cubic Goldstone cancellation of non-collinear magnets

questions.explanation: mode='dyson' is kept only as a diagnostic.

questions.question: Why are the source (all-annihilation) poles not broadened?

options.b: they are anti-resonant (negative energy): broadening them would leak an unphysical Im Σ at ω > 0

questions.explanation: Only decay and absorption channels can be resonant.

questions.question: Hands-on: sc_square(1.0) — Born maximum Γ on the grid (meV, 2 decimals)?
Hands-on: the same — self-consistent maximum Γ (meV, 2 decimals)?
questions.explanation: 1.30 meV: the self-consistent internal widths halve the extreme Born values.

questions.question: Hands-on: the same — mean self-consistent Γ over the grid magnons (meV, 2 decimals)?
questions.explanation: 0.56 meV vs the Born mean 0.96 meV.

questions.question: Hands-on: ⟨Γ_sc⟩/⟨Γ_Born⟩ for S = 3 (2 decimals)?
Hands-on: ⟨Γ_sc⟩/⟨Γ_Born⟩ for S = 100 (2 decimals)?
questions.explanation: ≈ 1: the Born limit is recovered for large S.

questions.question: Hands-on: at h = 0.75 h_s (just below the decay threshold) …

options.b: Born gives max Γ ≈ 1.0 meV (grid/threshold artefact), self-consistent ≈ 0.13 meV

questions.explanation: The threshold singularity of the Born result is removed.

questions.question: Hands-on: triangular AFM — near-Goldstone modes with the Lorentzian line shape …

options.b: become overdamped (Γ/E ≈ 2) — unphysical tails of the large off-resonant weights; the Gaussian keeps Γ/E < 0.01

questions.question: Which quantity measures self-consistency?

options.b: residual(): max |Γ − (−2 Im Σ(E))| with the converged internal widths

questions.question: What is Z in the output?
questions.explanation: Z < 1: weight transferred to the two-magnon continuum.

questions.question: How are widths at off-grid momenta (band paths) obtained?

options.b: periodic linear interpolation of the converged grid widths for the internal lines, then one evaluation

questions.question: Which CLI option switches on the self-consistent decay?
What does mode='dyson' do?

options.b: a diagnostic: real off-shell root with bare lines (mixes orders; breaks Goldstone near Goldstone modes)

questions.question: Which convergence check matters most for self-consistent widths?

options.b: the closed-grid size (and η): Γ is a BZ sum with discrete poles

questions.explanation: Closed grids are coarse; compare two grid sizes.

questions.question: Is the four-magnon damping Γ⁴ part of the self-consistency?

options.b: no — it is added on top (on-shell); the self-consistency treats the cubic self-energy

questions.question: What happens to the self-consistent result when S → ∞?

options.b: it approaches the Born result (relative corrections ∝ 1/S)
